predictions.justification: Recognizing a potassium emergency and selecting its management are sequential, independently scoreable decisions.
The approach to disorders of sexual development and diagnosis or management of hypoplastic left heart syndrome concern different conditions and pathways.
The pediatric-limp approach decision and all material state and categorical metadata are coextensive.
Reporting an adverse drug reaction and clinically classifying it are separate professional and diagnostic decisions.
Excluding alternative endocrine diagnoses and selecting PCOS management are sequential assessment and treatment decisions.
General prenatal-screening selection includes the benchmark's specified choice of group B streptococcal screening and other screening options.
Pediatric iron-deficiency anemia reasoning and age-specific injury-prevention counselling concern different topics and decisions.
General initial action for suspected aortic dissection includes airway, breathing, circulation, and perfusion support plus additional management scope.
The digital-health ethical-reasoning decision is unchanged; only the non-decision-changing confidentiality versus ethical-legal family wrapper differs.
Endometriosis management and retained-placenta reasoning concern different conditions and clinical pathways.
Differentiating benign, malignant, and systemic-associated skin lesions and managing lesions are separate diagnostic and treatment decisions.
Identifying patients at high colorectal-cancer risk for screening is a specified screening subdecision within the benchmark's broader screening-and-diagnosis scope.
The general chest-pain differential includes recognition of life-threatening features and adds other independently scoreable diagnostic scope.
Reasoning about refractory symptoms and performing a multidimensional suffering assessment are related but independently scoreable decisions.
Recognizing TAPVR as the cause of cyanosis and diagnosing TAPVR are the same diagnostic decision under non-decision-changing presentation wrappers.
Identifying protective factors informs but does not itself answer the integrated suicide-risk stratification decision.
Selecting CT follow-up for a solitary pulmonary nodule and recognizing airspace or parenchymal lung abnormalities are separate diagnostic decisions.
Initiating referral within the applicable gestational-age and access framework is one specified component of the benchmark's broader counselling-and-referral scope.
General end-of-life communication includes eliciting and documenting resuscitation and care wishes plus additional communication decisions.
Managing pulmonary imaging abnormalities and recognizing them are distinct follow-up and diagnostic decisions.
Both narratives target recognition of epidural hematoma from its biconvex appearance, but interpretation versus emergency-action metadata creates an unresolved modality conflict.
Routine diabetic-retinopathy screening and recognizing proliferative disease or macular edema requiring urgent referral are different stage-specific decisions.
The diabetes primary-care decision is unchanged; only the non-decision-changing complication versus preventive stage wrapper differs.
Selecting first-line statin intensity by risk is a specified initial-treatment subdecision within the benchmark's broader lipid-lowering therapy scope.
Diagnosing early pregnancy loss and managing or counselling for it are distinct clinical decisions with incompatible response modalities.
